content:
I'll be the first to admit my DIY iPhone camera mod looks a bit silly—but it actually makes shooting with my iPhone more practical and a lot more fun.

It started as a quick fix for a video shoot, but I ended up reaching for it far more often than I expected…

One of the biggest divides in the compact camera world is whether you actually need a viewfinder. Veteran camera fans used to argue endlessly about the merits of EVFs versus optical finders, but EVFs have gotten so good that almost nobody cares anymore.

But regardless of optical or electronic, a viewfinder has real, practical advantages over composing on the rear screen—especially when you're shooting in harsh sunlight. Even with the brightness cranked all the way up, it's hard to see what you're capturing in bright sun, and you may have to deal with screen reflections too.

It hasn't been a huge issue for me in London, but we've had record-breaking heat waves this summer, and honestly, it feels like thirty years since I've seen a cloud or a drop of rain.

For me, though, the reason goes beyond that. I find there's a different psychological experience between looking through a viewfinder at what's inside the frame versus looking at the world around it. Sometimes, that's the main reason I pick up a standalone camera instead of my iPhone.

When I chose a camcorder a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was clearly the hot pick, but the lack of a viewfinder gave me pause. In the end, I figured it wasn't a huge deal for me, since I mainly shoot indoors, and when I do need to shoot outside, rigging up a big screen with a sun hood basically solves most of the issues.

But sometimes I want something more portable than a fully rigged-out monitor setup, so I found a simple accessory that's great for outdoor use. It's a combination sun hood and loupe that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, essentially giving you an optical viewfinder.

I had an upcoming shoot where I'd be using both the BMPCC 4K and iPhone 16 Pro Max for video. I did a quick test on location, and the viewfinder accessory was incredibly helpful. Since the BMPCC 4K and iPhone have very similar screen sizes, I wondered if it would work on the iPhone too.

Of course, the iPhone doesn't have magnets to stick to, but the iPhone is so light that holding it against the loupe with my hand is no problem at all. What surprised me was just how well it worked, especially when I was using the Camera Control button as a shutter.

Since then, I've used the accessory in all kinds of situations—both for the practical benefit of being able to see the screen more easily in harsh sunlight, and for that feeling of being more immersed. My iPhone has long been my main camera, and with this DIY mod, I feel like there are even more situations where a phone is all I need.

Crazy or creative? Let me know in the comments. If you find it as useful as I do, unfortunately the exact one I bought seems to have been discontinued, and I haven't yet spotted anything similar designed for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, drop a link in the comments.
